CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for anxiety management and breast concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports significant anxiety in November and December that has resolved with current treatment on Buspar started by Dr. Brown. She describes the anxiety as severe during that period, starting during work hours and initially correlating with the week before her menstrual cycle, then progressing to random spikes. Patient notes she was started on Singulair by Dr. Ward during this time and was counseled that Singulair can cause anxiety. Patient attributes the anxiety to multiple stressors including a work "go-live" in November and December, leading the process of delivering COVID results to patients (with initial 9-day wait time), and opening evaluation centers and COVID clinics. She experienced guilt about her anxiety given she was not on the front lines. Patient stopped taking Camila birth control due to significantly increased hunger, and has lost some weight over the past six months. She continues to use vaginal cream once weekly for itching/discomfort and reports it helps. Regarding breast concerns, patient reports lumps in left breast that feel smaller but are still present and tender to palpation. She is concerned given her age (almost 40) and family history of breast cancer in mother at age 45.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current weight loss, though reports weight loss over past six months after discontinuing birth control. Denies itching or discomfort in genital area currently, though continues to use cream with good effect. Breast pain noted on left side. Denies other issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
History of abnormal Pap smear around 2009, required surveillance every six months initially with eventual return to normal. Last Pap smear was in 2019 and was negative/negative. Breast lumps/cysts. History of breastfeeding with clogged duct and soreness. History of progesterone use for menstrual regulation.

MEDICATIONS
Buspar
Singulair
Progesterone
Vaginal cream (for itching/discomfort; patient needs refill)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 45. Husband and daughter unvaccinated against COVID with concerns about long-term effects. Son received first COVID vaccine dose.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works in healthcare, leading COVID result delivery and clinic operations. Currently dealing with vaccine hesitancy within family (husband and daughter). Has one daughter and one son.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Neck: Small bumps palpated; patient notes they are smaller than previously.
Breasts: Left breast feels denser with tenderness noted inferiorly where patient had prior clogged duct during breastfeeding. Lumps palpable but patient notes they feel smaller; right breast unremarkable.
Genitalia: Appears good on external examination.

RESULTS
Pap smear in 2019 was negative/negative.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety: Currently well-controlled on Buspar. Will continue current regimen.
2. Breast lumps/cysts: Patient has had two menstrual cycles since progesterone initiation. Plan to continue monitoring. No change in appearance noted, which is reassuring. Offered referral to breast specialist for additional expertise and potential in-office ultrasound and faster biopsy capability if needed. Patient agreed to referral. Will send referral; specialist will contact within couple of business days to schedule.
3. Vaginal discomfort: Continuing vaginal cream use once weekly with good effect. Patient to obtain refill.
4. Pap smear: Will repeat given history of abnormal Pap in 2009 and increased concern for abnormal Paps in setting of stress/immunocompromise/potential COVID or vaccine exposure.
